paper.title: Towards Soft Fairness in Restless Multi-Armed Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: RMAB with Soft Fairness Constraint (two-state arms, known transitions, finite horizon)
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Restless (Markovian) bandit planning problem with known transition matrices; the guarantee is a value-iteration approximation bound, not a learning/regret guarantee (markovian environments are out of scope in v0.5).
unmapped: Each arm is a two-state MDP with known transition probabilities (planning, not learning)
States of all arms are fully observed
Objective is discounted cumulative reward over finite horizon with discount gamma, solved by softmax value iteration over episodes
Soft fairness: policy must not prefer an action with lower optimal Q-value
settings.definition_quote: There are $N$ independent arms, each of which evolves according to an associated Markov Decision Process (MDP)... we specifically consider a discrete RMAB where each arm has two states $\{ 0,1 \}$... At each time step $t\in[T]$, the algorithm can choose $k$ arms to pull according to observed states

bound.regime: k = 1, as number of episodes ep -> infinity

conditions: rewards in {0,1} per arm (total reward in [0, n])

source.label: thm:soft_bound
source.quote: Our \textit{SoftFair} method can achieve the performance bound as $\underset{ep\rightarrow \infty}{\lim \sup}V^{ep}(\mathbf{s})\leq V^{\ast}(\mathbf{s})$... $\underset{ep\rightarrow \infty}{\lim \sup}Q^{ep}(\mathbf{s},\mathbf{a}) \leq Q^{\ast}(\mathbf{s},\mathbf{a})$ and $\underset{ep\rightarrow \infty}{\lim \inf}Q^{ep}(\mathbf{s},\mathbf{a}) \geq Q^{\ast}(\mathbf{s},\mathbf{a})- \frac{n-1}{(2+c)(1-\gamma)}$

results.notes: Bound on the asymptotic suboptimality Q* - liminf Q^ep of the softmax value iteration (not a regret). Paper's n (number of arms) mapped to K. Also states limsup Q^ep <= Q*. Proof relies on a questionable Taylor step assuming 0<=delta<=1. Multi-arm (k>1) version with n-k is only a conjecture and not recorded.
